rulers.name: Estanislao Figueras
rulers.title: President of the Executive Power
rulers.note: Elected February 1873; on 10 June 1873 he left his resignation letter and went to Paris.

rulers.name: Francisco Pi y Margall
rulers.title: President of the Executive Power
rulers.note: Elected 11 June 1873; resigned 18 July 1873 'after just 37 days in office'.

rulers.name: Nicolas Salmeron
rulers.title: President of the Executive Power
rulers.note: Elected by 119 votes to 93 after Pi y Margall; resigned 6 September 1873.

rulers.name: Emilio Castelar
rulers.title: President of the Executive Power
rulers.note: Elected 7 September 1873 by 133 votes to 67; the Cortes recognised his defeat on 2 January 1874 (the Pavia coup follows in January 1874).

rulers.name: Francisco Serrano
rulers.title: head of the Unitary Republic
rulers.note: Formed a coalition government after Castelar refused to continue and 'proclaimed the Unitary Republic' (page: 1874); Juan de Zavala took over on 13 May 1874.

rulers.name: Juan de Zavala
rulers.title: head of government
rulers.note: Took over from Serrano on 13 May 1874.

rulers.name: Praxedes Mateo Sagasta
rulers.title: head of government
rulers.note: Took charge of the government on 3 September 1874.

keyframe_review.note: 984,999 km2 (bbox -84.8 to 145.0 E) is Spain plus Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines. The page gives no area, so the infobox check is not possible. Two corrections: (1) the shape runs 1873-1876 but the Republic ended on 29 December 1874 ('bringing an end to the Republic'), so 1875-1876 belong to kingdom-of-spain_1875; (2) the overseas provinces are held by the spanish-empire dossier (Cuba, where 'the Ten Years' War continued ... ongoing since 1868'), so the Republic is drawn as the metropole, as the kingdom-of-spain dossier draws the monarchy on both sides of it. Years: 1873-1874 only.

ledger.note: 1873: the Carlist rebels hold Catalonia against the Republic. the rebels 'controlled most of the Basque Country, Navarre, and Catalonia without opposition' (the page's sentence carries no year; it sits in the 1873 narrative after the cantonal rising; quote corrected by reviewer eu-20-n); the Third Carlist War was 'ongoing since 1872' (infobox of the war page: 21 April 1872 to 28 February 1876). Catalonia is the contested zone; the Basque Country and Navarre are the rebel state below.

region.text: Catalonia, where the Carlists 'controlled most' of the country in 1873

ledger.note: 11 February 1873: the First Spanish Republic is proclaimed in Madrid. Infobox 'Amadeo I abdicates: 11 February 1873'; 'On the next day a republic was proclaimed by a parliamentary majority' (the page's lead says 10 February for the abdication).

ledger.note: 12 July 1873: the Canton of Cartagena is declared. 'The Canton of Cartagena was declared on 12 July 1873'; the page also names cantons at Seville, Cadiz, Granada, Alcoy, Almansa, Torrevieja, Castellon, Salamanca, Tarifa and Algeciras, and provincial cantons in Valencia and Malaga, without dates; only Cartagena's is drawn.

region.text: the Canton of Cartagena, the naval base and its hinterland

ledger.note: August 1873: the Carlists take Estella and make it the seat of a provisional government. 'In August, Carlist forces captured the city of Estella', which became their capital under Carlos VII; in the Basque provinces and Navarre 'the Carlists managed to erect a temporary state'. The First Republic page says only that the rebels controlled most of the Basque Country and Navarre in 1873; the region is the researcher's reading (Gipuzkoa, Alava, Biscay and Navarre), the extent shrinks and grows in 1874-75.

region.text: the Basque provinces and Navarre held by the Carlist 'temporary state' with its capital at Estella

ledger.note: 12 January 1874: Cartagena surrenders. 'Cartagena resisted until 12 January 1874', after the Pavia coup of that month.

January 1874: General Pavia's coup ends parliamentary rule. The page calls it the 'January 1874 coup'; the Cortes had sat on 2 January 1874 and recognised Castelar's defeat; General Serrano then formed a government and 'proclaimed the Unitary Republic' (1874), a 'conservative republican dictatorship'. Same state, new regime; Juan de Zavala follows on 13 May and Sagasta on 3 September 1874.

December 1874: the Republic falls while the Carlist war goes on. 'In December 1874, a military coup installed a new Bourbon monarch'; the war ends on 28 February 1876 when Carlos VII leaves Spain, under the monarchy (kingdom-of-spain dossier). Catalonia is still contested on 24 September 1874 when 'Carlists still held the Basque Provinces and most of Navarre'.

region.text: Catalonia, Carlist-contested until the war ends in 1876

ledger.note: 29 December 1874: the Restoration ends the First Republic. 'On 29 December 1874 in Sagunto, General Arsenio Martinez Campos' proclaimed Alfonso XII, 'bringing an end to the Republic'; the Bourbon Restoration begins. The Basque-Navarrese Carlist state is still rebel-held and passes with the war to the kingdom.

wars.name: Third Carlist War

zones.text: the Basque provinces, Navarre and Catalonia, with a Carlist 'small state' in the Maestrazgo (Cantavieja) in 1874

wars.outcome: Government victory in 1876: Estella fell on 19 February 1876 and Carlos VII left Spain on 28 February 1876; the Republic held the war from February 1873 to December 1874 without defeating the Carlists, who besieged Bilbao from 21 February to 2 May 1874.
wars.note: Infobox '21 April 1872 - 28 February 1876'. The page's lead says the war 'began in 1871' in one sentence and 1872 elsewhere.

wars.name: Cantonal rebellion
wars.outcome: The Canton of Cartagena, declared on 12 July 1873, resisted until 12 January 1874; the other cantons are named but not dated on the page.

wars.name: Ten Years' War
wars.outcome: The Cuban insurrection, 'ongoing since 1868', continued through the Republic; the page records no territorial change in 1873-74 and Cuba is the spanish-empire dossier's land.
wars.note: Only the Republic's years are covered; the war's end is not on the page. No zone: the fighting was in Cuba, which the corrected shape leaves to spanish-empire; no metropolitan ground changed hands (reviewer eu-20-n).

certainty.note: The metropolitan frontier with France and Portugal is a treaty line; the Carlist-held north and east are soft zones that moved from month to month.

notes: Cliopatria's row runs 1873-1876; the Republic ended on 29 December 1874, and the kingdom-of-spain dossier already carries 1875-1876 as its own keyframe (kingdom-of-spain_1875). The overseas dependencies (Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, Fernando Po) are spanish-empire's; the page does not mention the Philippines, Fernando Po or Spanish Morocco. Counterparts needing dossiers: carlist-state (a rebel state that 'erected a temporary state' at Estella from August 1873 and held the Basque provinces and most of Navarre until February 1876: a type rebel dossier is warranted, and its dates are in this dossier's Third Carlist War page); canton-of-cartagena (July 1873 to January 1874, under one year: a counterpart string only). Page silent: the Republic's area; dates of the other cantons' fall; the Carlist extent month by month. The seven 'rulers' entries are the page's presidents and heads of government; the page dates Serrano's start only to 1874. The infobox area comparison could not be made.
